content.text:
Read-only findings:

- Backend uses domain models → service trait/implementation → repository trait → `ExposedDatabase` SQLx implementation → Axum handler. Rankings is the cleanest small example: `exposed/src/lib/{domain/models/rankings.rs,domain/services/rankings.rs,domain/repositories/rankings.rs,outbound/rankings.rs,inbound/http/handlers/rankings.rs}`.
- Routes live in `exposed/src/lib/inbound/http/routes.rs`. `AppState` has generic search/details/rankings services; adding a distinct service affects its generic parameters and handler bounds, server construction, plus state construction in outbound tests and `inbound/http/tracing.rs`.
- Search requires a ≥3-character term and ranks similarity; it is unsuitable for browse-by-month. Its domain `Entity` also embeds search-match provenance, so a dedicated browse identity model avoids manufacturing search metadata.

For month selection:

- `exposed.declarations.registration_date` is the source registration date. It is nullable `TIMESTAMPTZ`; use `[month_start, next_month_start)` in UTC. Do not use `created_at`, `updated_at`, or loader timestamps: those describe ingestion/storage operations.
- The importer converts source date-only registration dates to midnight UTC. `db/README.md`, “Timestamps,” explains this distinction.
- `CalendarYear` in `domain/models/entity_details.rs:226` provides a nearby typed-period pattern. A month type should own the UTC calendar boundaries, including December rollover. Pass a clock instant into period creation for deterministic tests.
- Include all declaration categories, including unknown IDs, and declarations with no funding entries when identifying MPs. Unknown dates cannot qualify.
- “MPs appearing this month” should deduplicate by `members.parliament_member_id`, not internal member UUID or name.
- Companies/funders require joining matching declarations to funding entries. Deduplicate canonical funder UUIDs, not names.

Canonical funder identity is important:

```sql
LEFT JOIN exposed.funder_alias_groups g ON g.funder_id = e.funder_id
LEFT JOIN exposed.funders f ON f.id = COALESCE(g.group_id, e.funder_id)
LEFT JOIN exposed.funder_group_names n ON n.group_id = f.id
```

Display `COALESCE(n.preferred_name, f.funder_name)` and link canonical `f.id`. This exact pattern exists in `outbound/rankings.rs:42`. Alias groups use a stable minimum-UUID group identity, with optional preferred display names. A raw entry funder ID could yield duplicate rows and inconsistent detail links.

`FunderKind` in `domain/models/funder.rs` is the canonical finite vocabulary. Existing rankings explicitly interpret “companies” as **all non-individual kinds**, including trusts, unions, unclassified funders, and registered parties. Its exhaustive match is in `domain/services/rankings.rs:111`. However, rankings restrict funder boards to `DonationSupport`; a current-month appearance list should not inherit that restriction. A shared classification method on `FunderKind` would prevent duplication if adopting the same companies vocabulary.

Frontend patterns:

- Standalone SSR route: `routes/rankings/+page.server.ts`, server-only API fetch/parser in `lib/server/rankings.ts`, serializable model in `lib/rankings.ts`, view in `routes/rankings/+page.svelte`.
- Landing browse entry points are in `LandingPage.svelte`; the shared shell currently has no primary navigation.
- Reuse `ResultRow`, native `.results-list`, caller-owned anchors, `.entity-text`, `.entity-name`, and `.entity-alias` from `lib/ui/COMPOSITION.md`. `ViewLinks`/`ViewLink` are available for category navigation; `Notice`/`MessageState` cover errors/empty results.
- `EntityIndicator.svelte` currently accepts search `Entity`, so either use underlying UI icons directly or make any reusable identity contract deliberate.
- Existing identity destinations are `/members/{parliament_member_id}` and `/funders/{canonical_uuid}`.
- Purple is MPs; teal is funders. No monetary totals are needed for an appearance list, which preserves the existing financial contract.

Verification/runtime:

- `outbound/rankings/tests.rs` shows SQLx migration-backed fixture tests plus real HTTP response tests. Useful cases: exact month boundaries, December rollover, null dates, unknown categories, declaration without entries, duplicate funding entries, two aliases mapping to one canonical funder, preferred names, non-individual kinds, and deterministic ordering.
- Frontend tests use `frontend/tests/backend.ts`: each worker starts a mock backend and actual built Svelte app, allowing SSR API mocks through `backend.route("**/api/…")`. `rankings.spec.ts` and `rankings-fixtures.ts` provide the closest examples. Gallery tests opt into development mode.
- Required UI checks: `npm run check`, `npm run build`, affected Playwright tests; desktop screenshots must be captured on the PR branch and attached to the PR.
- `psql` and `sqlx` are installed. Docker currently exposes `exposed-postgres-1` on `127.0.0.1:55432`, another project DB on `55434`, and the existing frontend on `5173`. I did not connect to or mutate databases.
- I made no file changes.
